hints.title: Distinct Characters as Bitmasks
hints.text: Because each word contains only distinct lowercase English letters, each word can be uniquely represented as a 26-bit bitmask integer.

hints.title: Store Start Masks
hints.text: Insert the bitmask of every startWord into a hash set for constant-time membership lookups.

hints.title: Test Removing Each Letter
hints.text: For each target word, turn off one bit corresponding to each character in the word. If the resulting mask exists in the startWord set, the target can be formed.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution

complexity.time: O(N) single pass or optimal algorithmic traversal
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing pairs of strings with anagram sorting takes O(S * T * L log L) which times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Integer bitmask hashing runs in O(S * L + T * L) time and O(S) auxiliary set memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Leverage bitmask representation for anagram invariance.
